correctness.rationale: The regular bipartite multigraph edge-coloring decomposition gives at most two unit switches per permutation layer. For a canonical three-cycle pair a 3-by-3 integer potential varies by at most 3 per switch and has endpoint gap 6n. Any pair sharing a positive cell admits a one-move first layer and hence distance <=2n-1. For disjoint supports three permutation matchings partition K3,3; either both matrices are pure disjoint permutation multiples or a mixed one admits an explicit three-move conversion of two layers, giving <=2n-1. Exactly six pure pairs are disjoint. The finite programs independently reproduce all distances for n=1..8.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves a natural sharp all-margin switch-distance question on balanced 3x3 contingency fibers, the smallest genuinely multidimensional Markov-basis model. It gives a uniform exact path bound with an intrinsic structural classification of all worst-case pairs, beyond standard connectivity and previous bounded censuses. This distinguishes unit-step integer fiber geometry from real polytope graph diameter and supplies a precise benchmark for transition-path algorithms; it does not claim mixing bounds.
